===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sek-}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}}
From {{inh|en|enm|signe}}, {{m|enm|sygne}}, {{m|enm|syng}}, {{m|enm|seine}}, {{m|enm|sine}}, {{m|enm|syne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|seġn|t=sign; mark; token}} and {{der|en|fro|signe}}, {{m|fro|seing||sign; mark; signature}}; both from {{der|en|la|signum|t=a mark; sign; token}}; root uncertain. {{doublet|en|signum|signal}}. Partially displaced native {{m|en|token}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}
[[Image:UragaIC.jpg|thumb|right|A [[traffic sign]]]]

# {{lb|en|countable|uncountable}} A [[visible]] [[fact]] that [[show]]s that something [[exist]]s or may [[happen]].
#: {{syn|en|indication|evidence}}
#: {{ux|en|Their angry expressions were a clear '''sign''' they didn't want to talk.}}
#: {{ux|en|Those clouds show '''signs''' of raining soon.}}
#: {{ux|en|Those clouds show little '''sign''' of raining soon.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=Although the Celebrity was almost impervious to sarcasm, he was now beginning to exhibit visible '''signs''' of uneasiness, the consciousness dawning upon him that his eccentricity was not receiving the ovation it merited.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|author={{w|Tony Hendrik|Dee Dee Halligan}}; Junior Torello|authorlabel=no|title={{w|What Is Love}}|album={{w|The Album (Haddaway album)|The Album}}|date=18 January 1993|artist={{w|Haddaway}}|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HEXWRTEbj1I|text=No, I don't know why you're not fair / I give you my love, but you don't care / So what is right and what is wrong? / Gimme a '''sign'''}}
## An [[omen]].
##: {{ux|en|"It's a '''sign''' of the end of the world," the doom prophet said.}}
## {{lb|en|medicine}} A [[property]] of the body that indicates a [[disease]] and, unlike a [[symptom]], can be detected [[objective]]ly by someone other than the patient.
##: {{ux|en|'''Signs''' of disease are objective, whereas symptoms are subjective.}}
# A mark or another symbol used to represent something.
#: {{syn|en|mark|marking|signal|symbol|token}}
#: {{ux|en|The sharp '''sign''' indicates that the pitch of the note is raised a half step.}}
#: {{ux|en|I gave them a thumbs-up '''sign'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2000|author=Geoffrey McGuinness; Carmen McGuinness|title=How to Increase Your Child's Verbal Intelligence: The Language Wise Method|publisher=Yale University Press|isbn=9780300083187|page=38
|passage=The sound of the Orlando dinner train whistle reminds me that it ' s already Friday, an auditory '''sign'''. Another auditory '''sign''', a distant thunder clap, warns me of limited computer time before our evening thunderstorm moves in.}}
# {{lb|en|North America|AU|uncountable}} Physical evidence left by an animal.
#: {{ux|en|The hunters found deer '''sign''' at the end of the trail.}}
# A clearly visible object, generally flat, bearing a short message in words or pictures.
#: {{ux|en|The '''sign''' in the window advertised a room for rent.}}
#: {{ux|en|I missed the '''sign''' at the corner so I took the wrong turn.}}
#* {{RQ:Macaulay History of England|chapter=3|passage=The shops were, therefore, distinguished by painted '''signs''', which gave a gay and grotesque aspect to the streets.}}
# A [[wonder]]; [[miracle]]; [[prodigy]].
#* {{RQ:KJV|Exodus|4|17|text=And thou shalt take this rod in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt do '''signs'''.}}
# {{lb|en|astrology}} An [[astrological sign]].
#: {{ux|en|Your '''sign''' is Taurus? That's no surprise.}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics}} Positive or negative polarity, as denoted by the + or - sign.
#: {{ux|en|I got the magnitude right, but the '''sign''' was wrong.}}
# A specific gesture or motion used to communicate by those with speaking or hearing difficulties; now specifically, a linguistic unit in [[sign language]] equivalent to [[word]] in spoken [[language]]s.
#* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=12|book=II|passage=And why not, as well as our dumbe men dispute, argue and tell histories by '''signes'''?}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Marcel Danesi|title=The Quest for Meaning
|passage=In American Sign Language (ASL), for instance, the '''sign''' for 'catch' is formed with one hand (in the role of agent) moving across the body (an action) to grasp the forefinger of the other hand (the patient).}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[sign language|Sign language]] in general.
#: {{ux|en|Sorry, I don't know '''sign''' very well.}}
#* {{quote-book|en |author={{w|Dorothy M. Johnson}}|year=1950|newversion=in |type2=book |editor2=|title=War Shirt|title2=Indian Country|location2=London |publisher2=Corgi|year2=1961 |page2=108|text="He don't talk English, only Cheyenne and '''sign'''." "You speak Cheyenne," Mason argued. "Why does he need an interpreter?"}}
# A [[semantic]] unit, something that conveys meaning or information (e.g. a word of written language); {{lb|en|linguistics|semiotics}} a unit consisting of a signifier and a signified concept. {{q|See [[w:sign (semiotics)|sign (semiotics)]].}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1692|author=Thomas Bennet|title=Short Introduction of Grammar ... of the Latine Tongue
|passage=A Noun substantive and a Noun adjective may be thus distinguished, that a substantive may have the '''sign''' ''a ''or ''the'' before it; as, puer, ''a boy, the boy''; but an adjective cannot, as, bonus, ''good''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1753|author=Charles Davies|title=Busby's English Introduction to the Latin Tongue Examined|page=11
|passage=A Pronoun is a Noun implying a Person, but not admitting the '''Sign''' ''a'' or ''the'' before it.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|author=Eero Tarasti; Robert S. Hatten|title=A Sounding of Signs: Modalities and Moments in Music, Culture, and Philosophy : Essays in Honor of Eero Tarasti on His 60th Anniversary
|passage=And some linguistic '''signs''', like “the”, “and” or “with”, may lack apparent objects, though they are clearly meaningful and interpretable.}}
# A [[military]] [[emblem]] carried on a [[banner]] or [[standard]].
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=6|passage=The great Ensign of Messiah blaz'd Aloft by Angels born, his '''Sign''' in Heav'n.|year=1873}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|signen}}, {{m|enm|seinen}}, {{m|enm|seinien}}, partly from {{inh|en|ang|seġnian|t=to mark; sign}} and partly from {{der|en|xno|en|seigner}}, {{m|en|seiner}} et al., {{uder|en|fro|signer}} et al., and their source {{der|en|la|signare|signāre|to mark, seal, indicate, signify}}; all from {{der|en|la|signum||a mark, sign}}; see Etymology 1, above. Compare {{m|en|sain}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# To make a mark
## {{lb|en|transitive|now|_|rare}} To [[seal]] (a document etc.) with an identifying seal or symbol. {{defdate|from 13th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|The Queen '''signed''' her letter with the regal signet.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[mark]], to put or leave a mark on. {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1726|author=Elijah Fenton|title=The Odyssey of Homer
|passage=Meantime revolving in his thoughtful mind / The scar, with which his manly knee was '''sign'd''' […].}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[validate]] or [[ratify]] (a document) by writing one's [[signature]] on it. {{defdate|from 15th c.}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|text=Enquire the Iewes house out, giue him this deed, / And let him '''signe''' it {{…}}.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} More generally, to write one's [[signature]] on (something) as a means of identification etc. {{defdate|from 15th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|I forgot to '''sign''' that letter to my aunt.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|_|or|_|reflexive}} To write (one's name) as a [[signature]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|Just '''sign''' your name at the bottom there.}}
##: {{ux|en|I received a letter from some woman who '''signs''' herself ‘Mrs Trellis’.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To write one's [[signature]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|Please '''sign''' on the dotted line.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To finalise a [[contractual]] agreement to work for a given sports team, record label etc. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
##*: Agents say Wales back {{w|Gavin Henson}} has '''signed''' for Cardiff Blues.
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[engage]] (a sports player, musician etc.) in a contract. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
##: ''It was a great month. I managed to '''sign''' three major players.''
# To make the sign of the cross
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[bless]] (someone or something) with the [[sign of the cross]]; to mark with the sign of the cross. {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
##* {{RQ:Book of Common Prayer|text=We receive this child into the congregation of Christ's flock, and do '''sign''' him with the sign of the cross.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1971|author={{w|Keith Thomas (historian)|Keith Thomas}}|title=Religion and the Decline of Magic|page=34|publisher=Folio Society|year_published=2012
|passage=At the baptismal ceremony the child was […] '''signed''' with the cross in holy water.}}
## {{lb|en|reflexive}} To [[cross]] oneself. {{defdate|from 15th c.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1855|author=w:Robert Browning|title=Men and Women
|passage=Shaking a fist at him with one fierce arm, / '''Signing''' himself with the other because of Christ.}}
# To indicate
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To communicate using a [[gesture]] or [[signal]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
##* {{RQ:Scott Guy Mannering|passage=I '''signed''' to Brown to make his retreat.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To communicate or make known (a meaning, intention, etc.) by a sign.
##* {{RQ:Melville Pierre|passage=Pierre signed his acquiescence, and Isabel proceeded:}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[communicate]] using [[gesture]]s to (someone). {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|He '''signed''' me that I should follow him through the doorway.}}
## {{senseid|en|use sign language}} {{lb|en|intransitive}} To use [[sign language]]. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To furnish (a road etc.) with signs. {{defdate|from 20th c.}}
# To determine the sign of
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To calculate or derive whether a quantity has a positive or negative sign.
